inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.85-0.9 gives cost of equity ~8.5-8.7%; EMTN/bank debt ~4.6% pre-tax (~3.4% after tax) at ~15% of capital (net debt + leases US$2.7bn vs ~US$17.5bn market cap) gives ~7.8%; rounded to 8.0% and applied UNIFORMLY to all three scenarios -- cyclicality, US repair-execution risk and pricing risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked in the discount rate (section 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (FY25 principal 138.8 + lease interest 47.6 = 186.4 = 2.8% of revenue; H1 FY26 76.8 + 23.3 = 100.1 = 2.8%) charged via lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT; lease liabilities (US$939.9m at 31-Dec-2025) EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY25 823.1 - 153.0 ROU = 670.1 = 10.0% of revenue) so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial at Brambles (no NCI line of consequence in FY2025 equity); no adjustment.
inputs.working_capital_note: wc_capture_pct -5: cash generated from operations trails Underlying EBITDA by ~US$90m/yr (FY25 2,197.9 vs 2,288.4) and H1 FY26 showed a US$46.9m working-capital outflow; a B2B rental business with receivables > payables consumes a little cash on growth. Small in size, negative in sign.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (FY2027-FY2036), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as a non-US cyclical operating company (asset-heavy pallet pooling; not a bank/REIT/LIC). First valuation of this ticker -- no memory entry. FY0 = FY2026, which is fully reported (20-Aug-2026) but NOT in the extracted filings: revenue 7,043 and Underlying Profit 1,494 come from the Analysis JSON; the FY26 EBITDA margin is estimated at ~33.8% (UP 1,494 + D&A ~885 from the H1 run-rate of 437.2) versus 34.3% in FY25, i.e. the ~US$90m Q4 US repair-capacity hit is inside the base. The FY2027 driver year is anchored to guidance issued with those results: revenue +2-4% cc, Underlying Profit +2-6% cc absorbing a US$35-55m residual repair headwind, FCF before dividends US$800-950m, pooling capex 13-15% of sales including incremental pallet purchases. TERMINAL: cap 18x owner FCF, essentially the Gordon multiple at 8%/2.5% (18.6x); mature compounder with ~21% ROCI justifies the full multiple, not the 12-15x cyclical discount. Disposal-proceeds treatment: capex is NET of recurring pooling-equipment compensation (~3% of revenue). CAPITAL-INTENSITY CAVEAT: net capex ran 22-27% of revenue FY18-FY23 and only fell to 14%/11% in FY24/FY25 under the asset-efficiency programme; the base holds it at 12% long run (FY27 guidance-consistent ~14% first), the bear reverts toward 13.5-15%. This single driver is worth more per share than the growth path.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 guidance (revenue +2-4% cc) and management's mid-single-digit medium-term proposition, decelerating; the 6.5% 3-yr revenue CAGR (FY22-FY25) embeds FY22-23 inflation price recovery that does not repeat, and FY2026 actual was +2% cc.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR diverges >30% from revenue/EPS in both directions (3-yr +11.0% vs 6-yr -2.1%) because equity is shaped by buybacks (US$0.4-0.5bn/yr) and the FY2019 IFCO disposal, not by retained growth -- not used as the growth anchor. FCF CAGRs are a capex-cycle artefact: owner FCF FY2022 was US$57.9m at peak pallet-purchase capex (net capex 27% of revenue) versus US$1,063.6m in FY2025 at 11%; they describe capital-intensity normalisation, not earnings growth.
historical_growth.notes: CAGR windows: 3-yr = FY2022->FY2025; '5-yr' is FY2019->FY2025 annualised over 6 years because FY2020/FY2021 annual rows are absent from the CSV (only H1 FY2021). Owner-FCF series used = OCF - capex + PP&E disposal proceeds - SBC: FY2018 388.6, FY2019 221.3, FY2022 57.9, FY2023 470.6, FY2024 851.6, FY2025 1,063.6 (lease principal not deducted in the history for lack of a consistent pre-FY2024 series; FY24 125.4, FY25 138.8). EPS 3-yr uses FY2022 41.9c -> FY2025 64.8c; EPS 'long' uses FY2018 43.5c -> FY2025 64.8c (7 years) because FY2019 EPS 92.1c carries the IFCO disposal gain.

base.growth_note: FY27 3.0% = midpoint of 2-4% cc guidance (no FX view taken); 3.5% FY28-31 is the low end of the mid-single-digit proposition (net new business 2-4% + price, less-than-zero like-for-like volumes); fades to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_note: FY26 est. 33.8% (Q4 repair hit inside). FY27 33.9%: UP +2-6% cc on revenue +2-4% is a flat-to-+0.4pp UP margin after the US$35-55m residual headwind. FY28 +0.6pp as the headwind lapses and repair capacity is rebuilt (mgmt targets stabilisation 1H FY27, +20% repair capacity by FY28); 35.0% plateau is +0.7pp above FY25's 34.3%, reflecting continued asset-efficiency/overhead productivity but no heroic operating leverage.
base.capex_note: NET of PP&E disposal proceeds (~3% of revenue). FY27 14.0% net (~17% gross) reflects guided pooling capex of 13-15% plus non-pooling capex plus the incremental pallet purchases to rebuild the US pool, and reconciles to the US$800-950m FCF-before-dividends guidance (model-implied ~US$0.9bn on the company's definition). Long-run 12.0% net sits between FY25's 11.1% and FY24's 14.1%, 2pp above D&A ex-ROU -- pool growth plus pallet-price inflation.
base.tax_note: 26% cash tax on EBIT (after lease and SBC). FY25 P&L ETR 27.4% of PBT; cash taxes paid ran 19-28% of PBT (FY23 214.7, FY24 311.7, FY25 257.3). EBIT is larger than PBT (net finance costs ~US$120m), so 26% of EBIT is ~28-29% of PBT -- slightly conservative vs the P&L rate. Pillar Two in scope from FY25; no ramp needed, no shelter being perpetuated.

bull.narrative: Top of FY27 guidance, then the full mid-single-digit proposition: like-for-like volumes turn positive as US/European consumer staples destocking ends, net new business runs 3-4% on single-use-to-pooling conversion, and price holds. US repair capacity is fixed on schedule (1H FY27) and the FY28 margin step-up is larger; digital (BRIX, serialisation) cuts asset losses so the asset-efficiency programme keeps net capex at 11% -- FY25's level held permanently. EBITDA margin reaches 36.5%, +2.2pp over FY25.

bear.narrative: The US repair-capacity problem is structural rather than temporary: labour and subcontractor churn keep service disruption going through FY27 (a third miss), customers in affected lanes defect to PECO or revert to one-way whitewood, and price realisation stalls as Brambles works to retain accounts. Like-for-like volumes stay negative (-1 to -3%, as through FY25/1H26), so revenue growth is price-only at ~2%. Higher pallet losses and replacement purchases pull net capex back toward 13.5-15% of revenue -- halfway to the 22-27% of FY18-FY23 -- and the EBITDA margin settles at 32.5%, below the FY26 trough. Not a solvency case: leverage stays inside the 1.5-2.0x target.

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 lands at the guidance midpoints (revenue +3% cc, UP +4%, FCF before dividends ~US$0.9bn on the company's definition) with the US$35-55m residual US repair headwind absorbed by efficiencies; repair capacity stabilises in 1H FY27 as planned and the FY28 margin recovers 0.6pp. Thereafter Brambles delivers the lower half of its mid-single-digit proposition (3.5% fading to 2.5%) with the EBITDA margin plateauing at 35% (+0.7pp vs FY25) and net capex normalising at 12% of revenue -- the post-transformation capital intensity is mostly, not entirely, permanent. The bull/bear axes are (1) whether the US repair issue is operational and temporary or a sign of structural service fragility, (2) whether like-for-like volumes ever turn positive, and (3) whether net capex stays at 11-12% or reverts toward historic norms.
scenario_narratives.bull: Repair fix on schedule, volumes turn positive, net new business 3-4%, margin to 36.5%, net capex held at FY25's 11% permanently.
scenario_narratives.bear: Repair issue persists into a third year with customer defections, price-only ~2% growth, margin 32.5%, net capex reverts to 13.5-15%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; bear lifted to 25% and bull cut to 25% because the company has missed its own guidance twice in one year on the same operational issue, the FY27 guide still carries an unresolved US$35-55m headwind, and April 2026 showed the problem recurring after it was declared addressed -- the bull case needs the repair fix, a volume turn and permanent low capital intensity to all hold at once. Balance sheet and franchise quality argue against going higher than 25% on the bear: leverage 1.13x, ~21% ROCI, defensive staples end-markets.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Brambles as a mature, capital-intensive compounder: unlevered owner FCF built from Underlying EBITDA less SBC, the full IFRS-16 lease cash and D&A ex-ROU, taxed at 26%, less capex net of recurring pooling-equipment compensation, discounted at a USD 8% WACC, terminal at min(Gordon 2.5%, 18x). The FY2026 US repair-capacity hit is inside the FY0 base, and FY2027 is tied to the guidance issued with those results rather than to a H1 FY26 run-rate. The valuation is far more sensitive to the long-run net-capex ratio (11-15% of revenue) than to revenue growth: every 1pp of permanent capex intensity is roughly US$100m of annual owner FCF, ~US$1.3/share at the terminal multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital intensity: the base assumes the FY24-25 asset-efficiency gains are ~permanent (net capex 12%); the FY18-FY23 record was 22-27%. Reversion toward even 15% removes roughly a third of the base value.
US repair-capacity execution: a third consecutive miss (recurrence after the 1H FY27 stabilisation target) moves the case toward the bear path and would justify raising the bear weight above 25%.
FY2026 balance-sheet vintage: net debt and share count are 31-Dec-2025; the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet is reported but not yet extracted. Refresh both when the FY2026 annual report is loaded.
FX: USD flows valued against an AUD quote at USD/AUD 1.4037; a 5% AUD move shifts every AUD per-share figure 5% with no change in the business.

Disposal proceeds (~US$220m/yr) are treated as recurring and netted from capex; if customer compensation for lost equipment falls with better asset control, net capex rises pari passu unless gross purchases fall too.
FY2026 EBITDA margin (33.8%) is estimated from Underlying Profit and a D&A run-rate, not read from the annual report.
